title: Active-active edge diversion with progressive degraded-paths and token-stitching for streaming sessions
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Hosted API customers see intermittent p95/p99 latency spikes and partial stream interruptions during cross-region maintenance and burst events. Current active-active routing shifts traffic abruptly, causing KV cache divergence, token loss for streaming sessions, and client-visible truncations.

Goal: Implement a coordinated active-active diversion strategy that preserves SLOs (p95/p99 latency and successful-stream-completion), provides safe degraded paths for tail events, and gracefully stitches short-lived session state (token/KV) when traffic is shifted between regions.

Scope: routing policy changes at edge/gateway, circuit-breaker thresholds and hysteresis, server-side token-stitch protocol for resumed streams, KV cache reconciliation guidance, telemetry gating for progressive shift, and a tested runbook for operator-driven and automated failovers.

Out of scope: long-lived state migrations, control-plane redesign, private deployment-specific RBAC changes (handled in a follow-up).

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Automated diversion can move up to 60% of in-flight sessions within 30s with <1% increase in stream-resume failures.
- SLOs: p95 latency increase <= 10% and p99 <= 25% relative to baseline during controlled switch.
- Circuit breakers trigger predictable degraded-path behavior and auto-recover within configured windows.
- Runbook validated in chaos tests with documented play-by-play and postmortem.

Notes on trade-offs:
- Strong session pinning reduces resume complexity but harms load distribution; we choose progressive partial-diversion to balance.
- Strict KV sync before cutover reduces resume failures but increases time-to-shift. We prefer token-stitch-first then background KV reconciliation for most workloads.

acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end automated diversion runbook executed in staging with metrics recorded in Datadog runbook dashboard. 2) p95 and p99 SLO breach windows recorded and reviewed; p95 <= +10%, p99 <= +25%. 3) Stream-resume failure rate <= 1.5% during progressive diversion tests at 60% traffic shift. 4) Circuit-breaker behavior documented: thresholds, backoff, and operator overrides. 5) KV reconciliation job completes without >5% request retries after finalization.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for token-stitch handshake and backward-compatibility.
- Integration tests: staged diversion with artefact recording.
- Chaos test: simulated region blackhole + progressive shift.
- Canary rollout: 2% -> 10% -> 30% -> 60% with automated abort on telemetry thresholds.
notes_on_implementation:
Key pieces: 1) Edge router change to support progressive multipath weights and 'resume-token' header propagation. 2) Lightweight token-stitch endpoint in runtime that can replay up to N tokens without re-executing full model. 3) Circuit breaker module with decaying counters and region-level quarantine that signals central controller. 4) Background KV reconciliation job that uses lease windows and conflict resolution by timestamp and token-anchor.

We intentionally avoid synchronous KV snapshotting to reduce cutover latency; instead accept short-lived cache misses and rely on stitch to preserve LLM prefix state for resumed streams.
